2607.05964.title: Umm... With Transformers? Insights from Filled Pause Use across Four Slavic Parliaments
2607.05964.paper_summary: Filled pauses (FPs) are a universal feature of spontaneous speech, yet most studies rely on small, single-language corpora, limiting the generalisability of their findings. We analyse ~4,000 hours of parliamentary speech across four related Slavic languages (Croatian, Czech, Polish, Serbian). FP occurrence is obtained via transformer-based automatic detection, while FP rate is modelled using Generalised Estimating Equations (GEE) with Mundlak correction to distinguish within- from between- speaker effects. We replicate a negative association of age and speech rate with FP rate, but find that gender effects are language-specific and directionally opposite to most prior literature. Novel analyses of sentiment, political orientation, and power status reveal a consistent positive association between sentiment and FP rate, alongside parliament-specific modulation by orientation and power status, with opposition speakers tending toward lower FP rates than governing coalition speakers.
2607.05964.paper_summary_zh: 填充停頓（FPs）是自發性言語的普遍特徵，但大多數研究依賴於小型的單語言語料庫，限制了其發現的普遍性。<lb/>我們分析了約4,000小時的議會演講，涵蓋四種相關的斯拉夫語言（克羅地亞語、捷克語、波蘭語、塞爾維亞語）。<lb/>FP的出現是通過基於Transformer的自動檢測獲得的，而FP率則使用廣義估計方程（GEE）進行建模，並進行Mundlak修正以區分說話者內部和之間的效應。<lb/>我們重複了年齡和語速與FP率之間的負相關，但發現性別效應是語言特定的，且方向上與大多數先前文獻相反。<lb/>對情感、政治取向和權力地位的新分析顯示，情感與FP率之間存在一致的正相關，並且在取向和權力地位上有議會特定的調節，反對派發言者的FP率傾向於低於執政聯盟發言者。
